questions.title: What does "constant height" mean?
questions.context: Today every widget grows with its content: the playground wraps with the text length, the stepper changes block-by-block per step (BpeStepper.svelte 473 lines), the comparison changes with the picked text. Article column is 680px (styles/tokens.css:127).

options.label: Same fixed height for all widgets
options.description: One shared value (e.g. about 640px on wide screens). Strongest visual consistency; some widgets will have spare room.

options.label: Fixed per widget, never changes while the reader uses it
options.description: Each widget reserves the height of its tallest state, so nothing jumps, but widgets can differ from each other.

options.label: Fixed height tied to the viewport
options.description: Widget is e.g. min(80vh, 720px) so it always fits on screen; same on every widget.

options.label: Custom
options.description: Describe in the box below.

questions.title: When content does not fit the fixed height
questions.context: Cases: a pasted long text in the playground, a long own-text in the comparison, the stepper pair table on a small viewport. Today the stepper pair table already scrolls in its own region.

options.label: Scroll inside the affected panel
options.description: Only the overflowing panel scrolls (keyboard-focusable region with a label). Everything else stays put.

options.label: Cap the input length
options.description: Limit typed/pasted text (e.g. a few hundred characters) so output normally fits; scroll only as a fallback.

options.label: Both a and b
options.description: Cap the input and scroll as a safety net.

questions.title: How wide may a widget go?
questions.context: Reading column stays 680px; widgets break out of it on wide screens. Chips and tables need room for two columns.

options.label: About 960px
options.description: Modest breakout, always comfortably inside a laptop window.

options.label: About 1120px
options.description: Room for two real columns; still centred with margin on 1440px screens.

options.label: Full viewport minus gutters, capped about 1280px
options.description: Widest; most content visible at once.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Breakpoint and the stacked fallback
questions.context: Two columns below the breakpoint would be cramped. The stacked layout is for narrower screens and phones (mobile is secondary per Phase 1 D-15).

options.label: Two columns from 900px; stacked below with auto height
options.description: Constant height applies only in two-column mode; stacked widgets grow with content for readability.

options.label: Two columns from 1024px; stacked below with auto height
options.description: Same rule, later breakpoint (tablets in portrait get stacked).

options.label: Two columns from 900px; constant height also when stacked
options.description: Stacked widgets keep a fixed height and scroll inside.

questions.title: Rule for what goes in the left and right column
questions.context: Playground: textbox, examples, counts, legend, tokens. Stepper: controls, why-sentence, chars stream, words, vocabulary, pair table. Comparison: picker/own text, two tokenizer rows, notes.

options.label: Left = input and controls, right = results
options.description: Same rule in every widget: you act on the left, you read the outcome on the right.

options.label: Left = the visual (chips, words), right = explanation (tables, notes, counts)
options.description: Visual first, numbers beside it.

options.label: Decide per widget
options.description: Planner chooses per widget within 'all information visible at once'.

questions.title: Headings and prose in the MDX: one section heading per widget?
questions.context: The wrappers fix heading ids because MDX-generated ids are fragile (research Pattern 4) and the wrappers also feed props (fixture subset for the playground, the licence-notices address from the site base). Moving to MDX means h2 ids and prop wiring move into the post. The pinned-sentence tests in post-content.test.ts must follow.

options.label: Plain ## headings in MDX, explicit ids where a widget needs aria-labelledby
options.description: Closest to 'all content in the MDX file'.

options.label: Plain ## headings, widgets labelled by their own aria-label (no heading id link)
options.description: Simplest; the widget names itself for screen readers.

options.label: Let the planner choose
options.description: As long as no .astro wrapper remains.

questions.title: Where do prop data and the base-aware URL come from once wrappers are gone?
questions.context: PlaygroundSection builds preTokens from comparison.json and passes sizeLabel; ComparisonSection builds noticeHref from BASE_URL. Svelte islands must not import the big fixture themselves (research Pitfall 6) and must not touch browser-only APIs at top level.

options.label: Post MDX imports data modules and passes props
options.description: Everything visible in the MDX; a little code in the post.

options.label: A small shared .ts module exports ready-made props; MDX only passes them
options.description: Keeps the MDX tidy. No .astro wrapper.

options.label: Planner decides

questions.title: How are text and token ID shown together?
questions.context: The stepper currently shows chips with the character on top and its byte value below (BpeStepper.svelte 'chars' stream). TokenDisplay has 'text' and 'ids' modes plus a TokenTable text alternative and TokenRows.svelte.

options.label: Each chip is two-line: token text on top, ID underneath
options.description: Like the stepper's character/byte stack. Wraps naturally with the text.

options.label: Chip with text; ID as a small label tucked under the chip, outside the outline
options.description: Cleaner chips, the ID reads as secondary.

options.label: Two aligned rows per line (text row, ID row)
options.description: Strong table feel; harder to wrap.

questions.title: Bytes and the text alternative after removing 'Peek under the hood'
questions.context: Phase 1 D-04: hex is shown on partial-character chips by default; the peek toggle revealed bytes for everything. The accessible TokenTable and the IDs toggle (D-08) also exist.

options.label: Keep hex on partial-character chips only; drop the toggle; keep the table alternative
options.description: Smallest change. Removes whole-string byte view.

options.label: As a, and the table alternative also lists bytes per token
options.description: Bytes stay discoverable for curious readers without a toggle.

options.label: Drop bytes entirely except where needed to avoid a replacement symbol
options.description: Hex still shown on partial chips (required by FOUND-06).

questions.title: Does the post prose about 'peeking' and the IDs toggle change?
questions.context: The playground lead-in and 'Takeaways' may mention the toggle and the peek switch; pinned sentences exist in post-content.test.ts.

options.label: Rewrite the affected sentences; update pinned tests together
options.description: Matches Phase 2.1 D-15 practice.

options.label: Rewrite and require another non-programmer read-through of those passages
options.description: Human-gated final task as in Phases 2 and 2.1.

questions.title: How do comparison and languages combine?
questions.context: Comparison: picker of five curated examples + own-text block (GPT-2 live, BERT after an explicit click showing its size) with a 'what to notice' note. Languages: static LanguagesTable.astro (sentence in six languages: bytes, GPT-2 count, BERT count) plus an optional 'Look inside' picker island (LanguagesDemo.svelte).

options.label: One picker: five examples plus six language lines; right side shows GPT-2 vs BERT cuts
options.description: Languages become more entries in the same list; a counts table sits under the cuts.

options.label: Two tabs in one widget: 'Texts' and 'Languages'
options.description: Keeps each view's own layout; one card, one height.

options.label: Left = picker, right = results; languages shown as a compact table in the left column below the picker
options.description: Everything visible at once, no tabs.

questions.chat_more: FINAL: Only languages. LanguagesTable and the "Look inside" picker (LanguagesDemo) become one widget; the comparison stays a separate widget. (Supersedes earlier "a" and the first note; ComparisonSection is not merged.)

questions.title: Is the languages table still the primary accessible form?
questions.context: Phase 2 D-14: a text-readable table is the primary accessible form for the languages demo. check-dist and e2e may rely on server-rendered output.

options.label: Yes: table stays visible and is server-rendered by the Svelte widget
options.description: Works with no JS and for screen readers.

options.label: Table stays but only in the accessible/text alternative; the visual form is chips or bars
options.description: More visual; table available inside the widget.

options.label: Planner decides, but a no-JS readable table must remain

questions.chat_more: Table stays visible and server-rendered inside the merged languages widget.

questions.title: Post heading and prose for the merged section
questions.context: Two H2s today: 'How does GPT-2 compare with other models?' (long prose with BERT/WordPiece/[UNK] explanation and citations 26-27) and 'The same sentence in other languages'. UPDATE after Q-11: comparison stays separate, so the two H2s stay; the open point is only whether the languages prose changes.

options.label: One H2 and one block of prose before the widget
options.description: Languages sentence is folded into the intro; widget follows.

options.label: Keep the two H2s; the single widget sits after the second prose block
options.description: Prose structure unchanged; one widget serves both.

options.label: One H2 with the BERT explanation above and a short languages note under the widget

questions.chat_more: Keep both H2s (comparison, languages); rewrite the languages prose only as the merged widget needs.

questions.title: How do we check the layout rules?
questions.context: Existing gates: Playwright e2e on the built site (e2e/), check-dist.mjs, vitest content tests. No iOS device. Constant height and breakout are visual rules, easy to regress.

options.label: Playwright assertions: widget height is identical across states at one wide viewport; stacked at narrow; no horizontal page scroll
options.description: Automated and repeatable.

options.label: As a, plus a manual visual check at 360, 768, 1024 and 1440px
options.description: Matches earlier human-gated checks.

options.label: Manual visual check only

questions.chat_more: Playwright height/overflow/no-horizontal-scroll assertions plus manual visual check at 360, 768, 1024, 1440.
